chunks: Abu Hamzah reported from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)
He said: Any Muslim who grants a concession to another Muslim in trade, Allah, the Exalted, will grant him an exemption from the chastisement of the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.إِقَالَة: Concession or forgiveness in a transaction/debt

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for forgiving a debt in Islam?
ai.summary: In the context of *Kitab al-Mumin*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of *iqa'ah* (forgiving a debt or claim) as a means of securing divine absolution from the punishment of the Hereafter. It reflects the Shia emphasis on interpersonal mercy (*mu'amalat*) as a direct pathway to spiritual purification, linking financial leniency with eschatological relief.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 125. Abu Hamzah reported that one of the two (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq) (a.s) said:
If any Muslim gives a concession to another Muslim in trade, Allah will grant him an exemption from the chastisement of the Day of Resurrection.
